business_description.value: Westlake Corporation manufactures and markets performance and essential materials, and housing and infrastructure products in the United States, Canada, Germany, China, Mexico, Brazil, France, Italy, and internationally. It operates through two segments, Performance and Essential Materials and The Housing and Infrastructure Products. The Performance and Essential Materials segment offers ethylene, polyethylene, chlor-alkali, chlorinated derivative products, ethylene dichloride, vinyl chloride monomer, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), epoxy specialty resins, and base epoxy resins and intermediaries. The Housing and Infrastructure Products segment provides residential PVC sidings; PVC trim and mouldings; architectural stone veneers; windows; PVC decking; polymer composite and cement roof tiles; PVC pipes and fittings for various water, sewer, electrical, and industrial applications; and PVC compounds for various housing, medical, and automobile products. This segment also offers consumer and commercial products, such as landscape edging; industrial, home, and office matting; marine dock edging; and masonry joint controls. It offers its products to chemical processors; plastics fabricators; small construction contractors; municipalities; and supply warehouses for use in various consumer and industrial markets, including residential construction, flexible and rigid packaging, automotive products, healthcare products, water treatment, wind turbines, and coatings, as well as other durable and non-durable goods. The company was formerly known as Westlake Chemical Corporation and changed its name to Westlake Corporation in February 2022. Westlake Corporation was founded in 1986 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas. Westlake Corporation is a subsidiary of TTWF LP.

historical_forecast_error.eligibility_note: Each observation is the consensus on the eve of the result — lead time ~0 — so it measures last-mile surprise: a cross-check on scenario severity and on how wrong late consensus has been. It is NOT a distribution of how far consensus moves over a holding period; that needs point-in-time consensus snapshots, which no Estimates Report carries. Each 'actual' is the figure CIQ's Estimates set against its own consensus, which is often NOT the line the financial statements report; `accounting_basis` names the filer's accounting STANDARD (US GAAP, IFRS), never the basis of that actual.
historical_forecast_error.usage_note: EBIT- or EBITDA-level shock today: error_per_forecast_revenue × today's revenue consensus. Revenue × margin scenario: the SAME year's Revenue pct_error and ratio_error, kept together. ratio_error alone answers how wrong the margin (or capex-intensity) forecast was, and multiplied by revenue it drops the revenue miss's effect. Exact identity: error_per_forecast_revenue = ratio_error + (actual ÷ actual revenue) × (actual revenue ÷ forecast revenue − 1).

midcycle_gap.read: The last twelve months' operating margin of 1.1% (CIQ EBIT) sits 8.7 points BELOW the 10-year median of 9.8% (EDGAR GAAP operating income) that R1 reverts to. R1 pairs that median with the median multiple from the same history, so an R1 value assumes a recovery to what the business was. If the decline is STRUCTURAL, that history overstates it; if it is a cyclical TROUGH, expecting recovery is right. On FY2025 the two sources differ by 12.5 points (GAAP a 14.1% loss vs CIQ a 1.6% loss): GAAP carries charges CIQ's EBIT excludes, and R1's median sits on the GAAP side — which pulls the median down toward the twelve months, so the difference narrows this gap rather than creating it: no reason to discount it, and if anything it understates it.
